_comment: Stryker — does the frontend suite actually bite?
The Rust half of this question is `cargo mutants` (.cargo/mutants.toml).
This is the fourth critical module, and the only one in TypeScript:
deltaProtocol.ts applies the server's incremental state updates to the
client's picture of the session. Everything the user sees is downstream of
it, and a wrong answer here is not a crash — it is a pane showing something
that is no longer true, which no test notices unless it was written to.
Scoped to that one file on purpose. Mutating the whole app would take hours
and report mostly on code whose correctness is not load-bearing; the point
is to find out whether the ~340 lines everything depends on are really
tested, not to produce a score.
Reading the result: a KILLED mutant is good — a test failed, so that line is
really tested. SURVIVED means the suite passed with the code broken, and
names a line nothing is checking. NoCoverage means no test even executed it.
Run it with `npm run mutants:ui` from the repo root. It is not a CI gate:
the useful output is the list of survivors, which someone reads and turns
into tests, not a threshold a build trips over. `thresholds.break` is
